body.p: These remarks are responsive to the Office action dated February 23, 2024. Prior to entry of this response, claims 1-20 were pending in the application. By way of this response, claims 1, 10, 12, and 16 are amended. No new matter is added. For example, support for the claim amendments may be found in the specification of the present application at paragraphs [0009], [0011], [0041], and [0043]. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application and allowance of the pending claims.

Unless the next action issued by the Office is a Notice of Allowance, Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner to contact the undersigned representative to schedule a telephonic Examiner interview to discuss whatever issues may still remain after entry of the present response.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 on the asserted basis that the claimed invention is directed to the abstract idea of a mental concept of evaluation without significantly more.
Applicant traverses this rejection.

While not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to further address the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection thereof. No new matter is added. For example, claim 1 is amended to specify that a non-transitory memory component comprises the first and second memory spaces, and further that the activity monitor software component is arranged to "cause the input to monitor a first event associated with the first software component," "cause the input to monitor a second event associated with the proxy software component," and "cause the output to generate an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events" (emphasis added).
Accordingly, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 as hereby amended and, thus, all of the claims depending therefrom, are all directed to eligible subject matter.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite.
Applicant traverses this rejection.

While not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the rejection of claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to specify that a non-transitory memory component comprises the first and second memory spaces, and further that the activity monitor software component is arranged to "cause the input to monitor a first event associated with the first software component," "cause the input to monitor a second event associated with the proxy software component," and "cause the output to generate an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events" (emphasis added).

Accordingly, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2-20 recite sufficient structure and, as such, the rejection of claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), first paragraph, as failing to comply with the written description requirement.
Applicant traverses this rejection.

While not believed to be required and solely for the purpose of expediting prosecution of the present application, and further without conceding the merits of the rejection of claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), first paragraph, Applicant submits that independent claim 1 is hereby amended to specify that the recited activity monitor software component is arranged to "cause the input to monitor a first event associated with the first software component," "cause the input to monitor a second event associated with the proxy software component," and "cause the output to

generate an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events" (emphasis added). Applicant further notes that dependent claims 9-12 each recite a sensor component, e.g., a wheel speed sensor component.
Accordingly, Applicant submits that the rejection of claims 1-20 under
35 U.S.C. 112(a) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), first paragraph, should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2016/0011932 (Abo El-Fotouh) in view of U.S. Patent No. 8,140,358 (Ling et al., hereinafter Ling).
Applicant traverses this rejection.
Independent claim 1 as hereby amended is directed to a system, and recites the following features:
an input;
an output;
a first software component for use in configuring operation of a
second software component via a proxy and stub interface;
a non-transitory memory component comprising:
a first memory space comprising the first software component, a proxy software component and an activity monitor software
component; and
a second memory space comprising the second software component and a stub software component; and
at least one processor for executing software components stored on
the first and second memory spaces,
wherein the activity monitor software component is arranged when
executed to:
cause the input to monitor a first event associated with the first software component;
cause the input to monitor a second event associated with the proxy software component, wherein the second event includes a command
event at the proxy software component;
assess compliance of the first and second events with a schedule of events, wherein assessing compliance includes checking order
and/or timing of the first and second events; and
cause the output to generate an error message in response to assessed non-compliance with the schedule of events.

Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references do not disclose at least a proxy and stub interface, proxy software component, and stub software component as recited by independent claim 1 as hereby amended. Applicant notes that the Office at pages 7-8 of the Office action primarily directs attention to paragraphs [0028], [0029], and [0033] of Abo El-Fotouh but Applicant respectfully submits that the cited portions of Abo El-Fotouh do not disclose the recited proxy and stub interface, proxy software component, and stub software component; rather, the cited portions of Abo El-Fotouh merely disclose various components and provide a very general description of software that has processes and subprocesses.

Furthermore, Applicant submits that the cited references do not disclose at least the monitoring of a first event associated with the first software component and monitoring of a second event associated with the proxy software component as recited by independent claim 1 as hereby amended. Applicant notes that the Office at pages 7-9 of the Office action again directs attention to paragraphs [0028] and [0029] of Abo El-Fotouh, and also to col. 11, 11. 1-13 of Ling, but Applicant submits that these portions of the cited references merely describe various components and discuss software generally and, as such, do not teach or suggest the monitoring of first and second events as required by independent claim 1 as hereby amended.

Because the purported combination of Abo El-Fotouh and Ling does not teach or suggest every feature recited by independent claim 1, Applicant submits that the 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2-20 should be withdrawn and such action is respectfully requested.

Applicant further submits that claims 2-20 are also independently patentable. For example, with regard to dependent claim 6 of the present application (i.e., specifying that the vehicle system is a cruise control system), the Office at page 10 of the Office action directs attention to col. 7, 1. 52 of Ling but Applicant notes that this portion of Ling merely lists "cruise control engaged" in a listing of "raw data elements" (see col. 7, 1. 15) with no actual suggestion as to an actual cruise control system.

Additionally, with regard to dependent claim 10 of the present application (i.e., specifying that the sensor component is a wheel speed sensor component), the Office at page 10 of the Office action directs attention to another portion of Ling (i.e., col. 27,

11. 10-17) but Applicant notes that, while this portion of Ling may describe the monitoring of vehicle speed, such monitoring is clearly for the purpose of determining acceleration/deceleration and storing data related thereto.

Applicant believes that this application is now in condition for allowance, in view of the above amendments and remarks. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner issue a Notice of Allowability covering the pending claims. If the Examiner has any questions, or if a telephone interview would in any way advance prosecution of the application, please contact the undersigned attorney of record.
Please charge any cost incurred in the filing of this response, along with any other costs, to Deposit Account No. 601570.
Respectfully submitted,
